displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The strongest divine-foundation case treats objective obligation as a relation between necessarily perfect practical reason, humanity's nature and ends, and God's rightful authority, rather than as mere conformity to an unexplained will.

novelty.explanation: This steelman repairs the circularity and missing-bridge weaknesses by adding practical-reason, authority, and human-end components.

premises.text: Some moral requirements purport to give every relevant agent reasons that do not disappear when personal desire, social approval, or immediate advantage changes.

novelty.explanation: This develops the transcript's universality claim while framing it in terms of stable agent-independent reasons.

premises.text: A necessarily perfect God would possess complete knowledge, perfectly ordered practical reason, and no conflict between moral understanding, intention, and character.

novelty.explanation: This integrates character and omniscience while avoiding the inference that outcome knowledge alone supplies value.

premises.text: If rational creatures are created with determinate capacities and ends, facts about their flourishing can provide objective reasons grounded in what those creatures are.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a natural-law bridge from creaturely nature and flourishing that was not articulated in the transcript.

premises.text: If God's prescriptions perfectly express those objective reasons, revelation communicates duties rather than making otherwise reasonless conduct obligatory by fiat.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the foundation-information conflation by making revelation communicative rather than arbitrarily constitutive.

premises.text: Rightful creative authority can add role-relative obligations of trust, gratitude, and stewardship when its exercise consistently serves the objective good of created agents.

novelty.explanation: This supplies qualified normative premises connecting creation and authority to duties without relying on power or punishment alone.

conclusion.text: Therefore, if necessary divine perfection, creaturely ends, and rightful authority are defensible, God can unify moral truth, knowledge, and obligation without reducing goodness to arbitrary command.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion proportionately states a conditional divine foundation supported by the repaired premises rather than assuming the disputed claims.

newArguments.title: Constitutive Reasons and Creaturely Ends
newArguments.text: A divine account can answer the is-ought objection by distinguishing brute descriptions from facts that are constitutive of agency. If rational creatures necessarily depend upon truth, coherent deliberation, mutual recognition, and stable social trust to exercise their capacities, then they possess reasons to protect those goods. God need not manufacture those reasons through commands; divine creation establishes the kind of beings involved, while perfect practical wisdom recognizes and communicates what their flourishing requires. This makes revelation evidential and authoritative without treating sheer power as morality.

novelty.explanation: This is a new natural-law and constitutivist bridge from agency and creaturely ends to objective practical reasons.

newArguments.title: Qualified Rightful Authority
newArguments.text: Creation alone does not entail obedience, but creation joined with perfect knowledge, unwavering concern for creaturely good, and legitimate governance may establish rightful authority. The relevant analogy is not ownership of an object; it is a fiduciary relationship in which authority is justified by competence, responsibility, and orientation toward the governed party's good. Divine prescriptions would then give agents additional role-relative reasons, while never converting harmful conduct into goodness merely because it was commanded. This directly answers the punishment-based caricature and places constraints upon what could count as divine authority.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the authority gap by making obedience depend on competence, responsibility, and orientation toward objective good.

thesis.text: The strongest secular case treats morality as disciplined inquiry into reasons that mutually vulnerable agents can justify to one another under impartial conditions, without requiring a divine truth-maker.

novelty.explanation: This steelman repairs the authority gap by connecting welfare and impartial construction to interpersonal justification.

premises.text: Conscious agents have empirically discoverable interests in avoiding severe suffering, preserving agency, maintaining trust, and accessing conditions necessary for meaningful choice.

novelty.explanation: This develops the welfare account into a plural set of interests rather than a single immediate happiness measure.

premises.text: A reason is not merely private when its supporting facts apply comparably to every similarly situated agent and survive correction for ignorance, coercion, and self-serving bias.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a general criterion for agent-neutral justification that was not explicitly stated in the exchange.

premises.text: Rules chosen without knowledge of one's social identity provide a practical test of whether principles distribute risks and protections impartially.

novelty.explanation: This develops the veil as a defeasible impartiality test rather than treating hypothetical agreement as automatically binding.

premises.text: Objective moral judgments can therefore concern whether conduct violates justified interests and impartial rules, even while the concepts used to describe morality remain conventional.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the chosen-standard limitation by connecting objective application to independently justified interests and procedures.

premises.text: Adding divine commands or character does not improve this justification unless an independent bridge explains why divine conformity supplies reasons to affected agents.

novelty.explanation: This extends the circularity and is-ought objections into a comparative explanatory requirement.

conclusion.text: Therefore, secular moral inquiry can support objective and revisable judgments through shared facts and impartial justification, while God's existence is not required for that limited achievement.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion proportionately claims defensible objective inquiry without claiming a final or exceptionless secular moral theory.

newArguments.title: Public Reasons Under Reciprocal Vulnerability
newArguments.text: Moral authority can arise from reciprocal justification among agents who are simultaneously capable of harming and being harmed. A proposed rule is deficient when it protects the speaker's interests while discounting equivalent interests of others without a relevant difference. This test is more than preference counting: evidence about pain, autonomy, dependency, deception, and institutional trust constrains which principles can be reciprocally defended. Because those facts remain true regardless of who occupies each social position, judgments based upon them can be objective in a practically important sense without requiring an external personal lawgiver.

novelty.explanation: This introduces reciprocal public justification as a new source of normative authority grounded in shared vulnerability.

newArguments.title: Independent Convergence as Evidence
newArguments.text: A secular account can treat convergence among distinct methods as evidence rather than making one chosen definition bear the entire foundational burden. Severe assault is condemned by welfare analysis because it predictably damages conscious interests, by contractualism because no exposed party could reasonably accept permission for it, by rights theory because it overrides bodily agency, and by rule analysis because tolerated violations destroy security and trust. Agreement across methods does not prove every verdict, but it reduces dependence on arbitrary stipulation and makes disagreement traceable to factual assumptions, weighting principles, or procedural defects that can be publicly examined.

novelty.explanation: This introduces methodological convergence as evidence against arbitrariness and as a framework for diagnosing moral disagreement.
